title: Director of Engineering - Risk and Compliance
description:
Company Description

We’re Checkout.com. You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day.


We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers.

Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale.

If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact.

With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started.

Role overview | Context

Checkout.com built its name serving the world's largest enterprises. We're now growing into many more types of customer: businesses of every size, including self-serve, startups integrating straight from our docs, and platforms (software companies, payfacs and marketplaces) that onboard thousands of sellers through our APIs. As our product range grows, that takes us from thousands of customers to millions.

At that scale, the decision about who we work with, and on what terms, can't be a manual review at the end of a sales process. It has to be a product. It decides how quickly a good business goes live, how much it costs us to serve them, and how confident our regulators and scheme partners are in us. We're looking for a senior Engineering leader to own that decision.

This team decides which businesses we can work with and on what terms. It covers business verification, screening, underwriting, ongoing monitoring and financial crime. It's a shared platform that serves every one of our businesses. Its users are our customers (directly, or through the platforms they sign up with) and, internally, our Risk, Compliance and Financial Crime teams and the analysts who run reviews and investigations.

Much of what we have today was built segment by segment and market by market, for a smaller number of large customers. The next chapter is one opinionated, configurable decisioning platform. Enterprise, platform and SMB customers should all run on the same foundations, with the right depth of checks and the right terms for each. That way a new product, segment or market doesn't mean rebuilding our controls, and this team isn't on the critical path for every launch.

Role overview | Risk, Verification & Compliance

The remit covers:

  • Risk decisioning: underwriting, risk tiering, exposure limits, reserves and settlement terms, and when to restrict or offboard, re-assessed across the customer lifecycle.

  • Business verification: company, ownership, document, bank account and website checks, run once for every segment.

  • Financial crime: sanctions and PEP screening, AML and transaction monitoring, and the controls, audit trails and reporting behind our regulatory obligations.

  • Decisioning platform: the shared infrastructure that runs these checks automatically for every market and customer type.

You'll partner closely with the teams that own onboarding and identity verification.

Role overview | Remit and Responsibilities

You'll be comfortable building and scaling critical platforms in a regulated environment, where correctness, auditability and availability matter as much as speed. You'll balance two goals that are often in tension: making it fast and easy for good businesses to work with us, and keeping bad actors out and the business compliant.

This is a change role. You'll assess what we have, set a clear direction, and move us from segment-specific, analyst-led processes to an automated decisioning platform, without pausing the business while you do it. You'll do this in close partnership with Product, Risk, Compliance, Financial Crime and Legal, and with the leaders of the businesses that depend on the platform.

You'll directly lead an established team of engineers and managers of varying seniorities. Amongst other duties, you'll have impact across:

  • Setting the technical vision and strategy for Risk, Verification & Compliance. That includes deciding what we build once and share, and what each segment, product or market configures.

  • Building a decisioning platform that automates the decisions that don't need a human, safely, and sends the rest to the right analyst with the context they need. Our automation rate sets our cost to onboard and to serve.

  • Making risk dynamic across the customer lifecycle. New businesses start on terms that match the signals we see: limits, reserves and settlement speed. Those terms relax automatically as the business trades well, and we act quickly when the signals change. This starts with simple rules and evolves into machine learning.

  • Making decisions explainable, so that customers, partners and our own analysts understand why a decision was made and what happens next.

  • Giving Risk and Compliance the dials. Acceptance criteria, early-life controls and policy should be configuration that can be changed, tested and measured by cohort, not a code change.

  • Keeping our financial crime controls ahead of growth. Screening and monitoring have to scale from large enterprises to a very large base of smaller businesses, through new channels, payment methods and products.

  • Leading the design and delivery of verification, screening, underwriting and monitoring systems that are accurate, auditable and highly available.

  • Representing Engineering in regulatory, audit, scheme and partner conversations where needed.

  • Managing and developing a high-performing team of individual contributor (IC) Engineers and Engineering Managers, providing guidance, support and career development.

  • Striving for best practice on hiring, coaching and enablement, and being a magnet for top talent.

Role overview | Desired Background, Core Competencies

The ideal candidate for the role will bring:

  • Experience leading multi-level engineering organisations (EMs and ICs) through growth and change, with a track record of developing leaders, not just hiring them.

  • A record of transforming critical platforms while the business kept running: multi-year re-architecture, migrations, or consolidating several systems into one.

  • Experience building and operating mission-critical decisioning or rules platforms at scale. Ideally these served several customer segments, products or markets from a shared foundation.

  • Experience in a regulated environment (financial services, payments or similar), where compliance, auditability and risk are part of the engineering problem.

  • Deep technical understanding of cloud-native, distributed and data-heavy systems, including how to run ML models safely in production.

Marketing Operations Team owns our marketing technology and tools, and the automation that supports go-to-market execution across our channels. This role works alongside Marketing Operations, with a different starting focus: improving the internal processes, workflows and systems that help Marketing plan and deliver its work. The aim is to 10x our impact.

This is a hands-on technical role in a marketing team. You’ll spend around 70% of your time building: understanding how work gets done, finding where it is manual or breaking down, and shipping practical solutions. You’ll partner closely with Marketing Operations to make sure what you build fits our existing tools and standards.

You’ll work across Marketing, in close partnerships across Marketing Operations, Commercial AI Transformation and the AI Centre of Excellence. You’ll bring a clear technical point of view on what is scalable and reliable, while making sure the systems you build are useful to the people who need them.

How You’ll Make an Impact

Find the problems worth solving

Work with teams across Marketing to understand their processes and the work behind their requests. Map workflows, identify manual effort, duplicated work, missing context and avoidable errors, then prioritise opportunities based on their potential value. You’ll use your creativity and judgement rather than simply build to a ticket.

Build AI-assisted workflows and integrations

Create and ship agents, automations, skills and integrations that make internal marketing work easier. You might use Claude Enterprise, Copilot Studio, Clay, MCP connectors, coding agents or other tools across our marketing stack. Work with Marketing Operations when a solution involves our marketing technology or channel tools.

Make internal marketing work more efficient

Build workflows that help teams do the work behind marketing more efficiently, from briefing, research and insight gathering to planning, content development and hand-offs. Connect information and tools so people spend less time on repetitive coordination and more time on work that needs their expertise. Partner with Marketing Operations where workflows touch marketing technology or channel execution.

Build systems people can rely on

Design beyond the individual task. Consider the data, context, tools, users, hand-offs, controls and feedback loops a workflow needs to work well. Identify where information is missing, where an agent needs better direction or where teams need support to use and improve the system.

Help marketers build with AI

Work alongside marketers to show what is possible and help them use AI with confidence. Create reusable patterns, skills, playbooks and guardrails so teams can solve more problems themselves and repeat good practice.

Test, learn and improve

Prototype and test workflows, learn from how people use them, and improve or retire them based on the results. Identify design, security, privacy, brand and scale risks early, and follow our AI governance and review processes.

Keep up with the tools

Stay curious about new models, coding tools, connectors and agent patterns. Be able to explain which tools are right for a particular job and why, whether you’re comparing Claude, ChatGPT, coding agents or emerging platforms.

What We’re Looking For

You build things

You’ve made working automations, prototypes, integrations, agents, internal tools or products, and enjoy taking a messy problem through to something people can use. Your job title matters less than what you’ve built and the value it creates.

You use AI hands-on

You use LLMs to get work done, not just to talk about what they could do. You’re comfortable prototyping with AI coding tools, testing different approaches, debugging and improving the result. You can show us something you’ve built with Claude, Codex, ChatGPT or another LLM platform, at work or in your own time.

You have sound technical judgement

You can reason about systems, APIs, data flows, permissions and failure modes. You understand the difference between a promising demo and a dependable workflow. You don’t need a traditional software engineering background, but you do need to be comfortable working directly with technical tools and making sensible implementation choices.

You understand marketing and GTM

You understand how demand generation, growth, customer marketing, marketing operations, sales and revenue processes connect. You’re familiar with concepts such as campaign briefs, segmentation, ABM, lead scoring, MQLs, MQAs, pipeline, attribution and lifecycle stages. You’re interested in the business outcomes behind the work.

You’ve worked across marketing or RevOps tools

You’ve built or supported workflows across platforms such as Salesforce, HubSpot, Asana, Clay or similar tools. You can think across a stack rather than optimise one tool in isolation, and you’re comfortable with connectors, APIs, webhooks or MCP-style integrations.

You know how to design useful workflows and agents

You can give a workflow the context it needs, choose the right tools, define hand-offs, involve people at the right points and make outputs easy to review. You understand that an agent’s performance depends on its data and operating environment as well as the model.

You prioritise for value

You can judge which problems are worth solving, which should remain manual and where a simpler answer will work better. You balance speed, quality, risk, maintainability and commercial impact, and can make a clear case for what to build next.

You measure and improve your work

You’re comfortable defining success measures, tracking usage and output, and deciding what to improve, stop or scale. You care about measurable gains in productivity, quality, speed or business impact.

You can hold the bigger picture while working through the details needed to ship.

You communicate clearly and bring people with you

You can explain technical ideas to marketers, commercial leaders, Product, Engineering, Security, IT and Operations in a way that helps them make decisions. You listen well, communicate simply and influence through your work and judgement.

You’re curious and self-starting

You’re comfortable with ambiguity and motivated to learn. You’ve taught yourself new tools, built something outside your formal remit or pursued a technical interest in your own time. A personal project, prototype, automation, community contribution or other example could show us how you learn.

You use AI responsibly

You might come from marketing technology, marketing operations, growth engineering, RevOps, automation engineering, product, full-stack engineering or another technical role close to commercial teams. title: Security and Compliance Engineer
description:
About Griffin

Hi, we’re Griffin. We’re a fully regulated UK bank that powers the accounts and payments offerings of product-led fintechs and platforms like Uber, Yonder, Prosper, and Sidekick. By doing the heavy lifting behind the scenes, our customers can focus on what they do best - delivering amazing customer experiences.

We’ve grown rapidly since our launch in 2024, and today provide the banking backbone behind products in remittance, payroll, wealth, insurance, proptech, payments, neobanking and more.

We’re moving into card issuing, stablecoin infrastructure, and agentic finance next as we continue to support the next generation of product-led companies.

Learn more about what we do

Our culture

We believe that smart, motivated, conscientious people thrive in high-trust, high-autonomy environments and have done our best to create such an environment at Griffin. People who thrive here don’t require much hand-holding, and go out of their way to figure out how to contribute in the most valuable way possible.

We've been remote-first since we were established in 2017 and we remain so today. Work here is asynchronous and fully flexible - because we want to be a part of your life in a way that helps you to get the most out of both your work and home life.

We understand that our culture and ways of working aren’t for everyone, and we’re very intentional about our hiring process as a result. We won't hire people who don’t seem like a strong fit for our core values, even if they're otherwise extremely qualified.

Our strong culture has helped us to remain a mission-driven company as we have scaled, and gives our people a clear, explicit operating framework and the space to focus on delivering real value for our customers.

Learn more about our culture.

The Team

The Craft function has seven small, cross-functional engineering teams - each with engineers, an engineering manager, and a product manager, working closely with designers.

You will work across the whole Craft function, with the remit of improving our controls and cyber security governance. You will initially work with and report to the Engineering Manager for Infrastructure as you establish yourself and take on your day to day responsibilities, additionally you will work closely with our CTO and Founder, Allen Rohner.

The Opportunity

We're looking for an Engineer 1.5 to become the engineering voice of security, compliance and assurance at Griffin. Sitting across engineering, security, risk and operational resilience, you'll turn standards and regulatory expectations into practical controls that engineers actually want to use and you’ll build those controls yourself, shipping code to production alongside the engineering team. You’ll also give our second and third lines real confidence in what we’ve built. It’s a rare hybrid role with broad ownership and a direct hand in strengthening Griffin’s security.

What Success Looks Like

In your first 6 months, you'll have taken ownership of our certification, attestation and audit work including ISO 27001 and SWIFT, with evidence organised and findings driven through to closure. Our engineering risks and controls will be well maintained, and our release, change and post-incident processes will be stronger. You’ll have shipped code that automates control checks and evidence collection, and you’ll be a regular contributor to our codebase.

By month 12 our resilience plans, including Important Business Service technical mapping, B& Continuity Planning and disaster recovery, will be current, and security and compliance will be easier to run and easier to demonstrate to customers, thanks to clearer ownership and smart automation.

To Do This You’ll Own

  • Control design and cyber security governance: translating standards into practical engineering controls and building and shipping the code that puts them in place, working with Engineering teams to get them live

  • Certifications and attestations, from SWIFT and FPS today to schemes like SOC 2 and ISO 27001 in the future, including the documentation behind them

  • Internal and external audits and customer due diligence requests, owning findings and driving them to closure

  • Engineering Risk and Controls Self Assessments, controls and actions, plus recurring control activity such as chaos testing and backup/restore

  • Code release and change management, improving the process and sampling releases to check adherence to policy

  • Post-incident reviews, including follow-up actions and sharing learnings with the right stakeholders

  • Engineering's contribution to operational resilience (DR plans and IBS technical mapping) and to managing engineering third parties alongside Operations

We expect you to shape this role

This description reflects what we need today. How you achieve these outcomes, where you focus your energy, how this role evolves—that's for you to define as you learn what our customers need and where our technical gaps are.

Your background

To ensure this, we're looking for people who have:

  • A hands-on engineering or technical background, including experience writing and shipping production code with an engineering-first approach to turning standards into practical controls and technical delivery

  • Experience in security, compliance, risk or assurance within a technical environment, including owning or significantly contributing to audits, certifications or attestations

  • Strong knowledge of compliance, risk and cyber security principles, and a broad understanding of change and release management, incident management, operational resilience and third-party governance

  • Sharp analytical and assurance skills: spotting gaps, assessing adherence to standards and following actions through

  • Stakeholder management and influencing skills across Engineering, SMEs, auditors and control functions, with a pragmatic, proportionate approach to governance

  • A love of writing - we have a major amount of written documentation that you will be contributing to, and we place a high degree of importance on clarity and readability (you can find out more here about how we write)

Ideally, you would also:

  • Be familiar with frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, SWIFT and FPS, ideally from a regulated fintech or challenger bank environment

  • Have used automation and code to improve security, compliance or control processes and documentation

What can we offer you?

We are an early stage startup and we're working hard to expand our benefits package. We're planning to add to this list in the future.

  • Remote-first flexibility: Work from anywhere in the UK

  • Work from abroad: Up to 20 days a year

  • Time off: 25 days’ holiday, bank holidays and a winter break (we shut down between Christmas and New Year)

  • Share options: Own a part of what we’re building together

  • Pension: Auto-enrolment into our Penfold scheme

  • Insurance: Private medical with Bupa (including family cover) and life insurance with AIG

  • Wellbeing: 1:1 coaching and therapy session available through Oliva

  • Family leave: Enhanced parental leave with up to 6 months on full pay after two years’ service

  • AI tools: Everyone has a Claude subscription on us and access to other premium tools

  • Your setup: We’ll support you in creating a comfortable and effective WFH environment.

As a bank, we’re committed to maintaining the highest standards of security. This means that the successful candidate will need to complete background screening, and our offer will be conditional upon satisfactory review of these checks. This would include verification of right to work, criminal record, credit history, social media and professional reference checks.

 

How do I apply?

Are we your next move? Apply via the link below, if there's a match our Talent team will reach out to schedule an initial conversation and talk you through what happens next.

We’re remote-first

We trust people to do great work wherever they are. We hire across the UK and most of our team works remotely full-time. We have a small London office in Moorgate for those who want it, and about a third of the company is close enough to use it occasionally, but there's no expectation to be there. What matters is the work, not where you do it.

Under representation

At Griffin, we’re looking for people who instinctively vibe with our values, behaviours and mission. You’re encouraged to apply, even if your experience doesn’t tick every box. Careers, like life, can take many twists and turns. Your technical expertise and path to where you are today will stand out. We're committed to creating a place where everyone belongs and we welcome diverse perspectives, backgrounds and people who are ready to build a global platform for programmable finance

title: Payroll Specialist
description:
Frontline work keeps the world running. Restaurants, hospitals, schools, nurseries, airlines, stores, emergency services. Together they employ 80% of the global workforce, over 3 billion people, and they're among the hardest businesses anywhere to run. By-the-minute scheduling, HR and payroll make them far more operationally complex than the average office, yet just 1% of venture funding has ever gone to software built for them.

 

Rising costs, wage increases, labour shortages and tighter regulation have made fixing that urgent. Sona is the AI-native workforce management platform for frontline organisations, with agents that match staffing to real demand and take the admin load off managers. That's a $500bn+ market the software industry has mostly walked past.

 

We've raised over $100M from N47, Felicis, Gradient and Northzone, signed more than 100 enterprise customers across the UK and US, and opened offices in London, New York, Austin and Lisbon. More on working at Sona here.

 

About the Role

 

We're hiring a Payroll Specialist to join Sona's payroll bureau, taking hands-on ownership of UK payroll processing for a portfolio of our customers.

Our bureau is growing fast. We're moving from around 15,000 payslips a month to roughly 22,000 by the start of Q4, driven by new customer go-lives in hospitality and care. That means the pace of the role is genuinely high, and we're hiring ahead of that curve rather than catching up after the fact.

Day to day, you'll manage a portfolio of standard and mid-complexity clients across multiple pay frequencies: statutory payments, pension auto-enrolment, HMRC filings and payroll journal reconciliation. You'll also handle client queries through our support desk, working to fast turnaround times. Your work is checked by a Senior Payroll Specialist before it reaches clients, as part of our standard quality process.

This isn't a conventional bureau role. Sona is a startup and the payroll team is still building its own processes and tools, so there's genuine room to shape how things work and to grow as the bureau scales. You'll be working on a product in a sector most software has ignored, and once you're through probation we support CIPP study through the apprenticeship levy.

 

Responsibilities

 

  • Own end-to-end UK payroll processing for a portfolio of Sona customers across multiple pay frequencies, covering standard and mid-complexity clients

  • Manage payroll queries through our support desk, giving clients fast, proactive updates and resolving within SLA

  • Process statutory payments, court orders, standard holiday pay calculations, Alabaster reviews and NMW checks for your own portfolio

  • Handle workplace pension auto-enrolment, contributions, reconciliations and submissions, flagging any miscalculated contributions for investigation

  • Upload, reconcile and submit payments across BACS, Faster Payments and SEPA, and manage payroll journal uploads and reconciliations

  • Manage HMRC filings (FPS, EPS) and year-end processing for your portfolio, escalating disputed or mis-allocated PAYE cases to your Senior or the Payroll Manager

  • Build strong working relationships with clients, including attending client meetings when needed, and flag product bugs to Engineering as you spot them

  • Spot and flag process gaps or improvements within your own portfolio, and support Payroll Assistants and Senior Payroll Specialists with day-to-day queries

 

Requirements

 

  • 2+ years hands-on experience processing multiple UK payrolls independently

  • Experience within a bureau or outsourced payroll environment is a bonus

  • Good working knowledge of UK payroll and tax compliance, including tax calculations and filing and payment requirements

  • Confident managing a busy queue of support tickets, with strong organisational skills and clear written and verbal communication

  • Comfortable in Excel (VLOOKUPs, pivot tables, concatenation) and Google Suite

  • Methodical and accurate under volume, and quick to flag issues rather than let them become problems

  • Bonus: CIPP or equivalent qualification, exposure to Irish payroll (PAYE, PRSI, USC), or confidence using AI tools in your day-to-day work

 

Benefits

 

  • Salary: £35,000 - £45,000

  • Hybrid working - 2+ days/week in our London office (Soho)

  • Share options

  • 35 days annual leave (25 days standard plus 10 flexible public holiday days)

  • Extra day of leave for every year of service

  • Pension contributions matched up to 5%

  • Comprehensive health insurance

  • Enhanced parental leave & pay

  • Salary sacrifice childcare scheme (Workplace Nursery)

  • Annual all expenses paid team retreats

  • The latest Macbook and equipment budget for your home office

  • Professional development budget

title: Test Development Engineer
description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecrafts for humanity.

Here at The Exploration Company, we are developing, producing, and operating Nyx, a modular and reusable space orbital vehicle that can eventually be refuelled in orbit, and which carries cargo – and potentially humans in the long run. We are also developing different types of propulsion systems to power our future vehicles and missions. As a talented Test Development Engineer, you will be part of the team that is responsible for the development of test facilities for our future propulsion systems.


Key Responsibilities / Tasks:

In your capacity as a Test Development Engineer, your role will be continuously evolving, but day to day your duties may include:

  • Synthesise test bench requirements from user and operator needs and plan required verification methods and tests.

  • Translate engine test objectives and stakeholder needs into facility-level functional and performance requirements.

  • Perform technical trade-offs to determine the best choice of hardware, software, equipment, component, location etc for various test facilities.

  • Perform risk assessment analyses for future tests and developing mitigation actions to ensure personnel and hardware safety.

  • Provide technical inputs to cost, schedule, procurement, commissioning, maintainability, and facility acceptance planning.

  • Prepare and maintain P&IDs of test facilities based on test bench requirements and selecting components.

  • Undertaking preliminary design of the ground support equipment with minimal oversight.

  • Undertake hazard assessments of the test facility design (FMEA and HAZOPs) to determine if any additional changes to the design are required.

  • Work with the current test bench team to coordinate end-to-end activities of the development of test facilities including design, reviews, manufacturing, installation, commissioning, test operations, ongoing upgrades and maintenance.

  • Work with procurement, AIT and design teams during the development of test facilities to find the right balance of technical solutions, cost and lead time.

  • Presenting findings to team members and participating in design reviews and project discussions.


What we would love to see from you:

  • Bachelor's, master's or PhD in aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related field (Master’s and above preferred).

  • 2–5 years of experience in propulsion, test facility development, experimental engineering, or a related field.

    • Practical experience in the design, development, commissioning, or operation of test facilities, preferably for rocket propulsion systems.

    • Experience in test facility design for cryogenic propulsion systems is highly desirable. Relevant experience with other cryogenic or high-pressure fluid systems will also be considered.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret technical data, challenge assumptions, and make evidence-based engineering recommendations.

  • Proven ability to work autonomously on assigned technical topics while contributing effectively to a multidisciplinary engineering team.

  • Excellent communication and leadership skills, with the ability to convey complex concepts to diverse audiences.

Why you should join us!

What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is:  

  • We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind 

  • We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them  

  • We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge?  

We'd love to hear from you if you wish to be a part of our journey. Please submit your CV now for immediate consideration and we will be in touch shortly.

title: Lead Tech SRE
description:
About Kestra

Kestra is the universal orchestration platform: open source, declarative, and designed to orchestrate data pipelines, IT automation, business workflows, and AI/agentic systems.

Trusted by over 10,000 organizations worldwide, including JPMorgan Chase, Bloomberg, FILA, and Crédit Agricole, Kestra orchestrates mission-critical workloads at scale. The open-source project has close to 30,000 GitHub stars, hundreds of contributors, and a fast-growing global community.

About the role

Kestra Cloud is our fully managed SaaS edition of Kestra. Each customer gets a dedicated Kestra instance on dedicated infrastructure, so the platform is a fleet of isolated stacks rather than one shared cluster. It is in Beta today, running production workloads for early customers, with General Availability planned for 2027. Each instance runs arbitrary user code (scripts, containers, queries against their own systems) through hundreds of plugins, and the fleet grows with every new customer. Provisioning, upgrading, and observing dozens to hundreds of identical stacks without drift is the core problem.

We're looking for a Lead Tech SRE to own Kestra Cloud end to end: the architecture and specs, the delivery, the monitoring, and the continuous improvement of the platform. You decide how the platform should evolve, write it down, split it into work, and ship it with your team.

You would lead a team of three, yourself included. That means you stay hands-on (a large share of your week is Terraform, Kubernetes manifests, and incident work) while setting the technical direction, reviewing designs, and dispatching work to two SREs.

You work closely with the CTO, the platform engineering teams building the Kestra core, and our security engineer. This is an engineering leadership role, not a people-management-only one.

What you would do

Architecture & specs

  • Own the target architecture of Kestra Cloud on GCP: the per-customer dedicated stack (cluster, network, databases, queues), how it is templated and versioned, regions, and the path from Beta to GA.

  • Write the specs (design docs, RFCs, ADRs) that turn product needs into infrastructure work, and defend the trade-offs: cost per customer vs isolation level, GCP project vs cluster vs node pool per customer, managed service vs self-run.

  • Define SLOs and error budgets per service and per tier, and make them the basis for prioritization.

Delivery

  • Break specs into work and dispatch it across the team, then review and unblock. You set the bar for Terraform modules, Helm charts, and GitOps conventions.

  • Automate the customer instance lifecycle: provisioning, upgrades, scaling, backups, migration, and decommissioning, with no manual steps.

  • Own the release path of Kestra Cloud with ArgoCD and GitHub Actions: progressive rollouts, rollback, and upgrade safety across the whole fleet of customer instances.

Monitoring & operations

  • Build the observability stack (metrics, logs, traces, alerting) so that issues are caught before customers report them.

  • Run on-call and incident response for the team: rotation, runbooks, blameless postmortems, and follow-ups that actually ship.

  • Plan capacity for a workload that is bursty by nature, and keep autoscaling honest.

Continuous improvement

  • Drive cost efficiency (FinOps) on GCP: per-customer cost visibility, right-sizing, committed use, and spot where it fits.

  • Harden the platform with our security engineer: network policies, workload identity, secrets, and audit trails toward SOC 2 expectations.

  • Feed back into the product: when Kestra itself makes the cloud hard to run, you write the issue, propose the fix, and work with core engineering to land it.

Our Tech Stack

  • Cloud: GCP (GKE, Cloud SQL, GCS, Cloud Load Balancing, IAM / Workload Identity)

  • Infrastructure as Code: Terraform, Helm

  • Orchestration: Kubernetes, Docker

  • Deployment & Repository: GitHub Actions, ArgoCD

  • Monitoring & Logs: OpenTelemetry, Elastic, Prometheus, Grafana

  • Datastore: PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch

  • Queuing: Redis, Kafka, AMQP

  • Programming language: Java, TypeScript (you read it; you don't need to write it daily)

What we are looking for

  • 8+ years in SRE, platform, or infrastructure engineering, including at least 2 years leading the technical direction of a team or a platform.

  • Deep, production-grade Kubernetes expertise: you have operated fleets of clusters at scale and know where they break (upgrades, configuration drift, networking, resource sizing).

  • Strong Google Cloud experience: GKE, IAM, networking (VPC, private clusters, load balancing), and managed data services. Equivalent depth on AWS or Azure is not a substitute here.

  • Expert Terraform: you have designed module structures and state layouts that scale to many identical customer environments, not just written resources.

  • Proven ability to architect, spec, and dispatch: you can show design docs you wrote, explain the trade-offs you made, and describe how you split the work and delivered it.

  • Real on-call and incident experience, including running postmortems and turning them into durable fixes.

  • SaaS operations background: you have run a product for paying customers, with SLOs that mattered.

  • Fluent in English and comfortable working autonomously in a fully remote environment.

  • Pragmatism: you pick the boring solution when it works and can explain why.

Nice to have

  • Experience running workloads that execute untrusted or user-defined code (sandboxing, gVisor, node pool isolation).

  • Built or operated a fleet control plane for per-customer environments (Kubernetes operators, Crossplane, GKE Fleet / Config Sync, or custom provisioning services).

  • FinOps practice on GCP: per-customer cost attribution, committed use discounts, spot node pools.

  • Exposure to SOC 2 or ISO 27001 audits from the infrastructure side.

  • Familiarity with workflow orchestration (Kestra, Airflow, Temporal, or similar) or the JVM in production.

Your first six months

  1. Month 1: take over the current architecture, audit the current Kestra Cloud architecture, and map the gaps between Beta and GA.

  2. Months 2 to 3: publish the GA architecture spec and the SLOs, agree on them with the CTO, and turn them into a roadmap the team can execute.

  3. Months 4 to 6: deliver the first GA milestones (one-click provisioning of a customer instance, observability coverage, safe upgrade path) with your two SREs.

  4. After month 6: drive continuous improvement of the platform, including a re-architecture of the first version of Kestra Cloud based on what Beta and the first GA customers taught us.

Perks & Benefits

  • Work from anywhere: We're a remote-first company, so you can work from wherever feels like home. Plus, you'll have access to coworking spaces worldwide if you ever need a change of scenery.

  • Health coverage: From medical support, dental, and vision, we've got you covered.

  • Home office setup on us: We'll provide all the equipment you need to work comfortably.

Our Hiring Process

We aim to move quickly (2-3 weeks), but we can adjust the timeline if needed.

  • Intro call with our CEO (30 min)

  • Technical scenario / Practical assessment (2 hours, asynchronous: write a short design spec for a Kestra Cloud scenario on GKE and Terraform, including how you would split the work across a team of three)

  • Architecture review with our CTO, walking through your spec and the trade-offs (45 min)

title: Lead Legal Counsel, Regulatory and Financial Services
description:
Are you looking to have an impact on the daily life of millions of entrepreneurs in France (and tomorrow in Europe)?

Are you looking for a work environment that values trust, proactivity, and autonomy?

Then Pennylane is the right place for you !

Our vision

We aim to become the most beloved financial Operating System of French SMEs and Accounting Firms (and soon, European ones).

We help entrepreneurs rid themselves of time-consuming tasks related to accounting and finance while providing them with access to key financial information to assist in making the best decisions for their business.

About us

Pennylane is one of the fastest growing Fintechs in France (and soon to be in Europe!)

In 5 years of existence, we’ve managed to :

💻 Make ourselves known as a groundbreaking accounting and financial software for small businesses and their accountants

💰 Raise a total of €400 millions, including from Sequoia, the famous fund from the Silicon Valley who invested early in companies like Google, Facebook, Airbnb, Stripe, Paypal and much more...

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Grow from 7 cofounders to 1000 happy Pennylaners : we’re now recognized as one of the greatest places to work in France (and also remotely), with a 4.6/5 rating on Glassdoor.

🌍 Build an international environment with more than 25 nationalities, with a strong remote-friendly culture, where 30% of the employees are already working from all parts of Europe

🤝 Earn the trust of thousands of customers and accounting firms and obtain outstanding ratings

🚀 Already more than 900,000 small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and over 6000 accounting firms use Pennylane in France!

We are currently operating approximately 30k business accounts under a BaaS model with Swan.

The role of Financial Services in our strategy is set to grow, both in terms of revenue and product contribution, to serve our 800k current customer base.

As such, we are initiating a process to get licensed as Etablissement de paiement et Société de financement. Our ambition is to start onboarding new customers by mid 2027 before starting migrating existing customers.

To meet this ambition, we are starting to hire our Tech, Product, Compliance, Legal and Ops leaders.

We are looking for a Lead Legal Counsel to drive the legal function of our Financial Services activity and build our regulatory legal team.

From the day you join until we are fully licensed, you will structure and execute the legal path to authorization: interpret requirements, translate them into an internal plan, and ensure deliverables are complete, consistent, and aligned across teams. You will help define the target operating model (intra-group and outsourced) and ensure it is legally defensible and well documented for the application.

After licensing, you will shift from “building the file” to running and scaling the legal function of the regulated entity: ensuring ongoing compliance with ACPR expectations, enabling product growth safely, and keeping the operating model (including outsourcing) continuously audit-ready. You will own the legal oversight of day-to-day legal and corporate matters (policies, governance, reporting support, inspections), lead the legal work for launching new regulated products and entering new partnerships, and manage the legal aspects of onboarding and migrating customers to the licensed subsidiary (terms, communications, complaints/conduct risk).

This is a greenfield project with high autonomy and responsibility, and the opportunity to shape the legal culture of a fast-growing fintech while managing and mentoring an experienced Legal Counsel, with the ambition to scale the team further as the business grows.

Organisation & Reporting

You will be part of the core Legal Department. Your reporting line will be Stanislas, our General Counsel.

You will manage a seasoned Legal Counsel and will be responsible for planning the future growth of the Financial Services Legal team. You will also partner closely with our Financial Services Chief Compliance and Risk Officer, Chief Operational Officer and the contract team.

Mission & Objectives

Team Leadership & Structuring

  • You manage, mentor, and develop your team member(s), fostering a high-performance, autonomous, and pragmatic legal culture.

  • You structure the team’s workload and roadmap, delegating effectively while remaining deeply hands-on.

  • You anticipate future hiring needs and actively participate in scaling the regulatory legal team.

Corporate and governance You design, document and run the legal aspects of corporate governance: delegation of powers, board/committee charters, conflicts management, inter-company arrangements on payment services outsourcing, governance narrative for the ACPR reports, and ongoing legal compliance cadence once authorized.

Products, contracts and customer legal architecture

  • You own the legal design of the FS product perimeter (payments services, account services, credit/financing products as applicable).

  • You work with the contractual team (Roland) on the associated contractual framework: customer terms, disclosures, pricing documentation, complaint handling language, and operational/legal flows (including KYC/AML handoffs, incident handling and customer communications).

Outsourcing / BaaS transition & vendor contracting You own legal matters relating to critical outsourcing and third-party reliance (including existing BaaS arrangements): contract negotiation, regulatory outsourcing clauses, audit/access rights, sub-outsourcing controls, exit plans, SLAs, data protection allocation, operational resilience expectations, and documentation suitable for ACPR scrutiny.

Migration readiness In close collaboration with the operation team (Maxime), you lead the legal plan for migrating customers from Swan (sequencing, consent/novation approaches, customer communications from a legal standpoint, continuity of mandates, handling of incidents/complaints, and safeguards to minimise conduct risk).

Privacy and Security In close coordination with our DPO (Léa) and security stakeholders, you ensure that our Financial Services operating model address data processing roles, cross-border flows (if any), retention, incident response, recordkeeping, and contractual protections with key providers.

Regulatory engagement support & internal enablement

  • Until we are fully licenced, you help prepare ACPR interactions (Q&A packs, position papers, meeting preparation).

  • Once authorized, you own the relationship with ACPR from a legal perspective, supporting the CCRO with legal opinions, advisory etc.

  • You train internal stakeholders on the legal/regulatory constraints that shape product and operations, and build a “legal-by-design” approach for Financial Services.

Culture, Training & Advisory You will be expected to operate as an owner, not a “support function,” and to produce pragmatic, regulator-ready outcomes.

About you

  • You have 8+ years of relevant experience, including in-house legal experience at a regulated entity (payments, EMI/PI, bank, lending/consumer credit, factoring, etc.), fintech, or BaaS.

  • You have a proven track record or a strong aptitude for managing, mentoring, and developing team members in a fast-paced environment.

  • You have substantial experience in regulated financial services legal work, and you are comfortable owning cross-functional programmes.

  • Senior legal expert in a French ACPR-regulated entity (établissement de paiement, établissement de crédit, société de financement or similar).

  • Hands on contract experience and knowledge about our regulatory environment (arrêté du 3 novembre 2014, PSD2, DORA, EBA Guidelines, etc).

Skills & mindset

Technical strengths You can credibly lead on :

  • ACPR/European regulatory frameworks for payments and/or lending/financing;

  • Outsourcing and third-party risk legal frameworks in regulated environments;

  • Governance and regulated-entity corporate law basics.

Soft skills

  • Player-coach mentality: capable of executing complex individual contributions while guiding and empowering your team.

  • You can work fast without losing rigour.

  • Strong pedagogy: able to explain complex regulatory legal topics to product managers, engineers and founders in simple, actionable terms.

  • Pragmatic, impact-driven approach, capable of operating under strong regulatory constraints without blocking innovation.

  • Very strong written and oral communication skills in both French and English.

Languages, presence and location

  • Fluent French and English are mandatory.

  • Based in France, with a strong preference for Paris.

  • Regular on-site presence in Paris is expected. Partial remote is possible. This is not a fully remote role.

Recruitment Process

1. Interview with Lucie (30-45 min), Senior Recruiter

2. Interview with Stanislas (1h), Head of Legal, Risk & Compliance

3. Case Study with Stanislas & Maxime (1h)

4. Last round with Laurent and Felix (45 min)

 

What do we do to make your work life easier

🌴 Wherever you are based, you will get 25 vacations days paid by Pennylane

💵 You’ll have a competitive compensation package

📈 You'll get company shares to enjoy a piece of the success story you're building with us

🏡 You’ll have a budget to turn your home into a more comfortable workspace, as well as a monthly allowance to work from a coworking space whenever you feel like it

⛹️ Through our partner Gymlib, you’ll have access to 8000 fitness spaces in Europe and more than 300 activities related to wellness

🇬🇧 You’ll have access to Busuu to perfect your English or your French

💻 You’ll get the latest Apple equipment

🏢 Depending on the teams and the requirements of the position - you'll be able to work remotely from your country of residence, as long as it is in Europe and within a maximum time difference of two hours from the CET time zone

🎉 We are committed to regularly coming together for company events such as Tech Days (which bring remote Pennylaners together every 3 months) or our annual company seminar, fostering significant moments of cohesion for everyone.

 

If you are based in France, you will have a French contract following French regulation on top of the additional perks : 6 to 12 RTT, 5 weeks PTOs, lunch credits (Swile), Alan Blue healthcare cover and regular events in cities where Pennylaners are mostly presents (Lyon, Bordeaux, Nantes…)

We're working on providing those last advantages to our people based outside of France as well, but it can be quite more complex depending on different countries.

 

Who are we looking for ?

To thrive at Pennylane, you need :

-To speak English (level is assessed and appreciated according to the department you’re applying to)

-To be energized by an ever-shifting work environment

-To be highly collaborative (within your team or other stakeholders)

-Sufficiently experienced to prioritize business-led actions on your day to day activity

 

We know that some people are less likely to apply than others, if they don’t feel like they meet the full list of criteria.

If you’re hesitating, we encourage you to apply : who knows, it might be the start of a meaningful and long-lasting collaboration.

 

Important information for candidates

Recruitment scam attempts are on the rise. We invite you to remain vigilant during your exchanges.

Applications through official channels only : apply exclusively through our job postings published on our official platforms (career site, official partner pages).

Always verify the sender's email address: our communications are sent from professional email addresses with the domains ----- or ----- style="min-height:1.5em">We will never ask you for payment or financial information

(bank details, payment for an interview, equipment purchases, etc.) as part of the recruitment process. If such a request is made to you, it is fraudulent. We invite you to not respond and to report it to us immediately.

title: Quantum Software Engineer
description:
Quandela is a global leader in quantum computing, designing, building, and delivering cutting-edge quantum solutions for research and industry. Its offerings include a very energy-efficient quantum computers for data centers, full-stack quantum computing solutions accessible via the cloud, and algorithm access services for academic and industrial customers. Following a pragmatic, step-by-step roadmap, Quandela has been deploying industrial-grade systems since 2023 while developing future generations of fault-tolerant quantum computers capable of scaling through the integration of thousands of photonic components. Quandela is committed to making quantum computing accessible to all in order to address the most complex industrial and societal challenges. Learn more at: Quandela | Leading Photonic Quantum Computing Solutions

Description of the Project

We are looking for a Quantum Software Engineer to develop the future software stack for controlling utility-scale quantum computers. At the interface of the theory and engineering teams, this ambitious project aims to develop internal tools to streamline the operation of logical quantum circuits on Quandela’s spin-photonic quantum computers.

This position requires a strong understanding of quantum computing protocols on real hardware, strong software engineering skills and proficiency with AI tools.

Your Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop a new compilation stack translating high-level quantum circuits into hardware-aware pulse schedules optimized for our photonic quantum computers.
  • Drive long-term architectural strategy, technical roadmap, and cross-organizational alignment.
  • Contribute to the development of a digital twin, receiving hardware instructions to simulate the behavior of our future QPUs.
  • Stay up to date with the latest developments in quantum software.

How You’ll Grow:

  • 3 months. By the end of the first quarter, you are expected to have a grasp over Quandela’s roadmap and specific approach to quantum computing. You understand how user operations are currently compiled to machine instructions and how that is expected to evolve
  • 6 months. By the end of the first semester, you have a firm understanding of Quandela’s technology and are already a key contributor to the compiler codebase for the near future
  • 12 months. You have a long-term vision over the quantum software’s activities, and are the owner of one or more work packages for strategic projects.

Requirements

What we're looking for: 

  • Master’s, or PhD in Quantum related field.
  • 2/4+ years of relevant experience in quantum software, quantum hardware automation, or related topics.

Must-have: 

  • A good understanding of photonic-based quantum computing.
  • Strong proficiency in python.
  • Experience working at the interface of software, experimental hardware, and theory teams in the industry or academia.
  • Collaborative mindset, able to serve as a bridge between various teams.

Important, but you can grow here: 

  • Proficiency in at least one system language (C++ or Rust)
  • Exposure to the quantum computing frontends and related ecosystem (e.g. cirq, qiskit, openqasm, cuda-q).
  • Hands-on experience with quantum photonic systems.
  • Familiarity with compilation mechanisms such as LLVM or compilation to microcode.

Benefits

  • Competitive salary, flexible based on your experience
  • Profit-sharing & company savings plan
  • 100% health coverage (Alan)
  • 50% transport reimbursement or sustainable mobility bonus
  • Meal vouchers (Swile), Gymlib fitness support
  • Childcare assistance & referral bonuses (€1,000–€2,000)

What we offer:

  • A meaningful role with real ownership, from day one
  • A team eager to collaborate and grow with you
  • A hybrid work model (3-4 days/week onsite in Massy, 1 day in Paris or 1 to 2 days remotely)
  • Daily exposure to the entire quantum stack — from high-level APIs to low-level firmware, and everything in between.

Process

  • Talent Acquisition Interview (30' - 45')
  • Hiring Managers Interview (45')
  • Use Case (a live use case or one to be prepared at home and presented afterward)
  • Meeting with the teams
  • 2 to 3 reference check

The internship will be conducted in the Photonic Integrated Circuits (PICs) department ofQuandela. The PICs team works on the production and development of the optical processors of Quandela quantum computers, having in mind performance and scalability.

At Orakl Oncology, we are accelerating the development of oncology treatments. Today, fewer than 5% of new cancer drugs succeed in clinical trials. Clearly, new methods are needed. We combine cutting-edge biology and AI to build the next generation of insight platforms with the world’s largest cohort of patient tumor avatars. These avatars fuel our AI-powered predictive engine, helping to anticipate clinical trial outcomes, validate therapies, and uncover new drug candidates. By generating multimodal, real-world data, we deliver insights that consistently outperform existing solutions.

Our mission is simple yet ambitious: to bring more effective treatments to patients who need them - and to make drug development smarter, faster, and more personalized. The company is growing fast, and we are now seeking the best talents to come and join our exciting and ambitious team in the fight against cancer - join us!

Position overview

Orakl Oncology works on a large cohort of patient-derived organoids (PDO) to predict clinical outcomes of patients and derisk clinical trials. We are looking for a dynamic and motivated Lab Technician to help us execute large-scale drug screening assays on our semi-automated platform, either for internal or external projects. In this position, you will:

  • Actively participate in our commercial contracts: you will take care of numerous PDOs of interest and perform drug screening assays to generate high-quality, robust datasets. These results will be leveraged by our data science and computational biology teams to deliver actionable insights and decision-support data to our partners.

title: AI Product Concept Designer & Interior Stylist – Home Décor (Part-/Full-time)
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an AI Product Concept Designer & Interior Stylist – Home Décor (Part-/Full-time) based in France.

In this fully remote role, you will combine creative vision, interior design expertise, and advanced AI image-generation skills to develop distinctive, commercially promising home décor products. You will transform emerging design trends and customer preferences into original product concepts and compelling visual experiences. A key part of your work will involve creating photorealistic interior scenes that showcase products with accurate materials, textures, colors, and proportions. You will collaborate with designers to refine concepts and prepare product visuals for e-commerce launches. By balancing aesthetics with commercial potential, you will help shape an attractive product portfolio for a premium home décor brand serving online customers. This long-term freelance opportunity offers the flexibility to work part-time or full-time while contributing directly to product innovation and digital merchandising. It is ideal for a visually driven creative professional who understands how to turn inspiring design ideas into products customers want to buy.


Accountabilities
  • Product concept development: Research interior design trends, competitor offerings, and customer preferences to identify new home décor opportunities and develop original, commercially viable product concepts.
  • AI-powered concept visualization: Use advanced generative AI tools to explore, visualize, and refine new physical product ideas, translating creative concepts into compelling visual representations.
  • Interior styling and scene creation: Place existing and proposed products into realistic, aesthetically cohesive AI-generated interiors that reflect different design styles, including Japandi, organic modern, and coastal interiors.
  • Photorealistic product imagery: Produce high-quality lifestyle and product visuals for e-commerce websites, ensuring generated images accurately represent the original products' shapes, proportions, materials, colors, and textures.
  • Visual quality and consistency: Maintain high standards of realism, composition, lighting, and styling across all creative outputs, ensuring that product details remain faithful to the intended designs.
  • Trend research and opportunity identification: Monitor emerging interior styles, materials, product categories, and customer preferences to uncover opportunities for new product development and commercial growth.
  • Cross-functional collaboration: Work closely with designers and relevant team members to refine concepts, incorporate feedback, and prepare product designs and visual assets for launch.
  • Commercial evaluation: Assess the market appeal and potential sales value of proposed products, balancing aesthetic originality with customer demand and commercial objectives.
  • E-commerce content development: Create visually engaging product and lifestyle imagery that strengthens online merchandising, communicates product value, and supports customer purchasing decisions.
  • Creative workflow management: Organize multiple projects, manage deadlines, maintain clear communication, and deliver consistent, high-quality outputs in a fully remote working environment.
  • Product feasibility awareness: Consider practical manufacturing requirements, material limitations, production constraints, and shipping considerations when developing physical product concepts.

    • Requirements

  • Visual design and aesthetic expertise: Excellent visual taste and a strong understanding of interior design, styling, color theory, materials, textures, proportions, and composition.
  • Advanced AI image-generation skills: Demonstrated proficiency with generative AI tools such as Nano Banana, Flux, Adobe Firefly, Midjourney, or comparable platforms.
  • Photorealistic image creation: Proven ability to generate convincing interior scenes and product imagery while preserving accurate product characteristics, including shape, material, color, texture, and proportions.
  • Creative concept development: Strong imagination and the ability to translate market insights, design inspiration, and customer preferences into original, visually appealing, and commercially promising physical products.
  • Relevant portfolio: A portfolio demonstrating high-quality interior visuals, AI-generated imagery, product concepts, home décor projects, or other closely related creative work.
  • Project management and organization: Strong organizational skills, reliability, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple creative assignments while meeting deadlines.
  • English proficiency: Fluent English communication skills for collaborating with the team, discussing concepts, understanding feedback, and documenting creative decisions.
  • Commercial awareness: An understanding of how visual design, product differentiation, and customer preferences influence purchasing decisions in e-commerce.

    • Strongly preferred:

  • Professional experience in home décor, interior styling, furniture, or lifestyle products.
  • Experience developing concepts for physical products from initial inspiration through visual refinement.
  • Familiarity with US interior design trends, home décor preferences, and target customer expectations.
  • Experience producing product photography alternatives, lifestyle visuals, or marketing imagery for e-commerce websites.
  • Knowledge of wood, natural finishes, and other materials commonly used in premium home décor.

    • Nice to have:

  • Experience collaborating with manufacturers, product designers, or suppliers.
  • Understanding of product feasibility, manufacturing processes, production constraints, and shipping considerations.
  • Experience using Pinterest, Instagram, or similar platforms to research interior design inspiration, consumer trends, and emerging product opportunities.
  • Familiarity with iterative creative workflows that combine AI-generated concepts with product development and commercial evaluation.

    • Important role clarification: This position focuses on AI-assisted product concept development, interior styling, and photorealistic visual creation. It is not a traditional CAD design or UX/UI design role. The ideal candidate combines outstanding visual judgment with the ability to create attractive, realistic, and commercially viable home décor concepts using generative AI.

    Benefits

  • Competitive compensation: US$25–$45 per hour, depending on experience, skills, and portfolio quality.
  • Flexible engagement: Choose between part-time and full-time collaboration, with an expected workload of approximately 25 hours per week.
  • 100% remote work: Work remotely from Anywhere.
  • Long-term opportunity: Initial 12-month contract with an emphasis on sustained collaboration and continued product development.
  • Freelance flexibility: Independent contractor engagement, offering flexibility in organizing your work and managing creative projects.
  • Creative ownership: Contribute directly to product concepts, interior styling, and visual assets that support commercial launches.
  • AI-driven innovation: Work with modern generative AI tools to explore new creative workflows and develop innovative product imagery.
  • Cross-functional collaboration: Partner with designers and other team members to refine concepts and bring new home décor products to market.
  • Portfolio development: Build experience creating AI-powered product concepts and high-quality lifestyle visuals for a premium direct-to-consumer e-commerce business.

    • Application requirements:

    Please include the following when applying:

  • Your portfolio featuring relevant interior visuals, product concepts, AI-generated images, or home décor projects.
  • A list of the AI image-generation tools you regularly use.
  • Your expected hourly rate.

Depending on your profile and interests, you will focus on one of these topics:

Have the Modeler write a specification of a formula (what it should do, and the tests it must pass), then build a small Formula Writer model that produces a correct formula from it.

2. Building Models from External Documents

Turn amorphous inputs (long PDFs, call transcripts, existing applications, templates) into structured Pigment applications: write the tests first, then iterate on a DSL representation until they pass.

Given an existing database, determine which blocks and transformations to create to make sense of the data and integrate it as a Pigment model.

Les collections femme et homme font référence à l’art de vivre à la française et aux gestes universels de beauté, intégrant des influences allant de la photographie d'art aux arts décoratifs, en passant par le cinéma, la peinture et la sculpture.
 
Au fil des années, Jacquemus a mis en scène ses défilés dans des lieux uniques et inattendus, notamment une piscine parisienne, le Musée Picasso, un champ de lavande en Provence, un champ de blé aux abords de Paris, un marais salant en Camargue et une plage à Hawaï. description:

High blood pressure is the world's most common disease, causing 18M deaths each year. At Hilo by Aktiia, we're building a world where no lives are lost to its effects — with technology that helps people take control of their health. 

We're a venture-backed scale-up with $96M raised from investors in Europe and the US. Rooted in 18 years of research at the Swiss Center for Electronics and Microtechnology (CSEM), our device is the world's only medically accurate, cuffless, continuous blood pressure monitor for daily use — clinically validated and CE Marked as a Class IIa medical device, now available in 12 countries. In July, we launched in the US. 

We're a remote-first company headquartered in Neuchâtel, Switzerland, united by our passion for impact and innovation. Applicants must already hold a valid visa or work permit for their country of residence, as Hilo is not able to provide visa sponsorship.


Role Overview

As Influencer Marketing Manager, you will develop and run Hilo’s influencer marketing program across our key markets. You will find creators whose voices and audiences fit our brand, negotiate effective partnerships, and shape content that makes Hilo relevant and credible. The role combines brand and performance: you will use data to estimate the potential of each partnership before we invest, measure its results, and apply what you learn to future campaigns.

Work location: Our company operates on a remote-first model. This role can be performed remotely from anywhere in Europe. Fluent English and German are a must. Occasional travel to our office in Neuchâtel, Switzerland, or to team events may be required.

Core Responsibilities

  • Identify, assess, and recruit creators across relevant platforms and markets.
  • Develop campaign concepts that balance Hilo’s brand goals with measurable commercial outcomes.
  • Forecast likely reach, engagement, traffic, and acquisition outcomes to guide creator selection and budgets.
  • Negotiate fees, deliverables, timelines, and content usage rights, including rights to use creator content in paid campaigns.
  • Manage partnerships end to end, from briefing and content review through publication and reporting.
  • Build and nurture long-term relationships with creators and brand ambassadors to drive sustained awareness, trust, and advocacy.
  • Collaborate with paid media teams to amplify high-performing creator content across paid social and other relevant channels.
  • Set clear goals, track brand and performance metrics, and compare results with initial estimates.
  • Use campaign data and audience insights to improve creator selection, content formats, and investment decisions.
  • Work across marketing and product to align campaigns with Hilo’s priorities and approved health claims.
  • Build repeatable processes that support growth across the US, UK, Germany, and other markets.

Requirements

Background & Experience

  • At least 2 years of hands-on influencer or creator marketing experience, including managing partnerships from start to finish.
  • A data-driven mindset: you can estimate campaign outcomes, assess performance, and turn findings into better decisions.
  • Strong creative judgment and an understanding of how creator content builds both brand trust and customer demand.
  • Strong negotiation skills and confidence working with creators and their representatives.
  • Excellent communication, organization, and attention to detail.
  • Fluency in English; German is a plus.
  • Experience in health tech, wellness, medical devices, or another category where trust and accurate claims matter is welcome.

Benefits

What Makes You A Great Fit

At Hilo by Aktiia, our values guide everything we do: 

Move the Needle — You focus on what truly drives impact for our customers and company. You use data and clarity to guide your decisions and prioritize what matters most. You push boundaries with bold, thoughtful innovation and hold yourself accountable for results.

Move Fast, Learn, Refine — You work with urgency and purpose, balancing speed with high quality. You treat mistakes as learning opportunities, experiment thoughtfully and iterate quickly. You take ownership, act hands-on and always look for smarter, faster ways to get things done, including leveraging AI and new tools.

Team First — You put the team above individual interests, building trust through openness and respect. You encourage healthy debate, challenge directly while caring personally and stand behind team decisions. You act as an owner, stepping in when needed and doing what’s necessary for the team’s success.

Why Join Us?

  • Hilo by Aktiia is becoming one of the most important med-tech companies and you can be part of this exciting story.
  • Work on a mission that matters: transforming cardiovascular health at global scale.
  • Be part of a high-impact, fast-growing, and venture-backed scale-up company.
  • Collaborate with a diverse, passionate and talented team.
  • Competitive compensation, equity program and other benefits (depending on location).

Ready to Move the Needle?

If you are passionate about making a meaningful impact in people's lives and excel in an environment where individuals take ownership and are committed to delivering results, we are happy to receive your application.

title: Team Lead - Invoices
description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous!

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

About the role

Invoices is BLP's largest product. Every day, it decides whether a supplier invoice can be posted to the customer's ERP without a human touching it. The invoice team builds and runs that product.

This is a leadership job with three parts that are equally important:

  • Build the team. The team is growing fast and is distributed across Zurich and several European countries. You hire, onboard, and grow engineers, and you develop the subteam leads who will carry more of the line management as we scale.

  • Deliver for our biggest customers. Some of the largest enterprises in Europe are rolling out BLP right now. Their go-lives, automation rates, and escalations land on your desk, and you make sure the team delivers on what we promised.

  • Turn the team into an empowered product team. Today, a lot of work still arrives as requests through proxies. You lead the shift toward a team that owns its problem space, defines outcomes, measures them, and decides what to build.

As Engineering Team Lead for Invoices, you lead the team that owns BLP's invoice product: You own the team's roadmap, delivery, people, and hiring.

This job is for you if you want to lead a strong engineering team through its next phase of growth and own the result.

You report to the Director of Product Engineering and work closely with the other product team leads, product management, and the go-to-market organization (project managers, customer success, and sales). The team is organized in subteams, each with its own lead, and you are the person who keeps them aligned.

What you'll do

Lead and grow the team

  • Run regular 1:1s, ensure growth of the engineers in your team, review progress, and make promotion and ranking decisions together with engineering leadership.

  • Coach and develop subteam leads, and set up the subteam structure as the team grows.

  • Keep a distributed team connected and productive: clear working agreements, transparent planning, and a culture where people raise problems early.

Hire

  • Own hiring for the team end to end: define the profiles, screen candidates, run interviews, review coding challenges, and close offers together with Talent Acquisition.

  • Keep a high bar while hiring at pace (our current target is around two new engineers per month), and make sure every new joiner has an onboarding plan and a buddy.

Own the roadmap and priorities

  • Build the quarterly roadmap and run monthly planning with product owners and product management, prioritizing by customer impact, revenue, and strategic value.

  • Balance enterprise go-lives, automation improvements, platform migration, developer experience, operations, and new products, and say no when something does not move the product forward.

  • Escalate early and clearly when priorities conflict, and communicate decisions to the go-to-market organization.

Deliver for strategic enterprise customers

  • Take responsibility for the engineering side of large enterprise go-lives: requirements engineering, solution design, test and fix cycles, and go-live readiness.

  • Work directly with project managers and, where needed, with customer stakeholders and their IT teams, and give clear, regular engineering updates.

  • Close gaps in the product rather than per customer, so the next enterprise customer arrives on a platform that already handles their case.

What you'll bring

  • You have led an engineering team of 8+ people for at least two years, ideally in B2B SaaS, and you have grown a team through hiring rather than only inheriting one.

  • You have a strong backend engineering background and can still read, review, and discuss production code and system design with senior engineers.

  • You have hired many engineers yourself, you know what a high bar looks like, and you can run a structured interview process.

  • You have delivered complex software for enterprise customers, including demanding go-lives, and you are comfortable in a room with customer stakeholders.

  • You prioritize ruthlessly, communicate trade-offs clearly, and can hold a position with engineers, sales, and executives while keeping the relationship.

  • You develop people: you give direct feedback, set measurable goals, and help engineers grow into leads.

  • You take ownership, surface problems early, ask for help when you are stuck, and hold your team to the same standard.

  • You are fluent in English. German is a strong plus, since many of our customers and colleagues are in the DACH region.

What you'll get

  • A real mandate. You own the invoice team end to end: people, hiring, roadmap, and delivery.

  • Impact you can measure. Automation rates and go-lives on our largest accounts are directly visible to customers and to the business.

  • A strong team. Engineers from serious academic and industry backgrounds who care about doing the work well, with subteam leads already in place.

  • A smooth handover. The current team lead moves into a new role in engineering leadership and stays available to support your start.

  • Room to grow. As a fast-growing, global AI company, BLP keeps creating new leadership opportunities.
